scope: Uganda pilot: source-reviewed reference directory, all original major-road candidates and named workbook locations

global_scope_policy.purpose: A manageable global inventory of crossings on main roads, with bounded exceptions for the closure research.

targeted_exceptions.reason: One of the four principal Kenya–Uganda road entry posts in the official Kenya list; its mapped approach is secondary. Retain this documented major-post exception.
Explicitly named in closure record GL13. Retain the two unresolved road-contact alternatives for targeted location review; this does not authorize a general minor-road survey.

limits: OSM road classes vary between countries and are not traffic-volume measurements.
A named documented major post or named workbook crossing can be reviewed as an explicit exception, with its reason and sources retained.
Existing smaller-road and rail findings remain background data; they do not expand the global extraction scope.
Even a main road can follow a border or intersect inaccurate boundary geometry. Topology and source checks still apply.
The reference list is not a complete inventory of all formal or informal crossings.
Supported correspondence means named crossing and mapped route agree; no surveyed positional accuracy or current operation is claimed.
Unknown candidates prevent an honest global precision/recall estimate. Recovery is reported against this dated, non-exhaustive benchmark only.
All review uses AI-assisted desk research and automated checks; it is not independent human validation.
Geometry review groups are not crossing-facility counts. Border alignment and exact gate questions remain explicit.
Closure dates and canonical workbook facts are unchanged. All new references remain outside the public map.
